newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- quiet, off slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- quiet, off slightly.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were slightly lower at midday, following Treasury securities lower in quiet Monday action, traders said.
One trader quoted the bid side unchanged to off about one to two basis points, but said activity levels are extremely light. "It looks like the dealers took the day off for May Day," the trader said.
U.S. Treasury prices were sagging even more, with market participants attributing the erosion to a correction from last week's big rally.
The government long bond was down 13/32 at 96-13/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
Also weighing on fixed income markets are this week's auctions. The Treasury is set to sell $17 billion of 3-year notes Tuesday and $12 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday.

Supply in the municipal market this week is expected to total $4.1 billion in 102 sales, the largest dollar total since $4.5 billion was offered the week of April 7, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings for the week were expected to total $3.3 billion in 42 sales, with a $486 million San Antonio, Texas, deal through PaineWebber Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 60 sales totaling $749 million are on the schedule. A $173 million Tennessee deal on Wednesday is the largest.

In the muni secondary, Dade County, Fla., water and sewer FGIC 5-1/4s of 2026 were were bid at 5.72 percent, down one basis point from Friday. Port Authority of New York and New Jersey JFK International Air Terminal MBIA 5.75s of 2022 were unchanged at 5.94 percent.
June municipal bond futures were down 1/32 at 114-29/32, while June Treasury bonds edged down 3/32 to 109-26/32. The MOB spread widened to 163 ticks from 161 at the close Friday.
